title: The Psychological and Physiological Effects of Light and Colour on Space Users

findings.antecedent: Exposure to different coloured lights (Blue low, Blue high, Green low, Green high, Red low, Red high, Natural) compared to white light
findings.consequent: Mean Heart Rate (HR) of all subjects
findings.mechanism: The variation of HR in response to colour and lighting conditions is not significant when considering the average HR of all the subjects for each colour light.
findings.quote: The results show a very hight p-value for all colour lights (p>0.31 for all colour lights).

findings.mechanism: HR is different from one person to another, leading to significant inter-subject variation.
findings.quote: The results are p=0.00 when taking person as a factor

findings.mechanism: The change in HR is not significant when considering the average HR of all subjects under each colour light.
findings.quote: p=0.27 when taking colour as a factor.

stimuli.description: Participants were exposed to different light and colour conditions by illuminating a 1.5m x 2m white non-reflecting screen with floodlights that had globes of green, red and blue colours. Eight different colours and light intensities were used: White (207 Lux), Blue low (28 Lux), Blue high (48 Lux), Green low (90 Lux), Green high (169 Lux), Red low (92 Lux), Red high (157 Lux), Natural (20-105 Lux).

limitations: This research has not studied the difference between the response to different colours and light intensities based on gender and age.
